In [[mathematics]], the '''Hessian group''' is a [[finite group]] of [[order of a group|order]] 216, introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Jordan|authorlink=Camille Jordan|year=1877}} who named it for [[Otto Hesse]]. It may be represented as the [[group (mathematics)|group]] of [[affine transformation]]s with [[determinant]] 1 of the affine plane over the [[finite field]] of 3 elements.<ref>Hessian group on [http://groupnames.org/index.html#?Hessian GroupNames]</ref> It has a [[normal subgroup]] that is an [[elementary abelian group]] of order 3<sup>2</sup>, and the [[quotient group|quotient]] by this [[subgroup]] is [[isomorphic]] to the group SL<sub>2</sub>(3) of order 24. It also acts on the [[Hesse pencil]] of [[elliptic curve]]s, and forms the [[automorphism group]] of the [[Hesse configuration]] of the 9 inflection points of these curves and the  12 lines through triples of these points.

The triple cover of this group is a [[complex reflection group]], <sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub> or {{CDD|3node|3|3node|3|3node}} of order 648, and the [[direct product of groups|product]] of this with a group of order 2 is another complex reflection group, <sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub>[4]<sub>2</sub> or {{CDD|3node|3|3node|4|node}} of order 1296.
